doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Tough years after leaving Mingus
summary: After leaving Mingus around 1972, working on his own was harder, especially in the late 1960s and after.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Has there been a period of years that were the toughest to make a living as a jazz musician for you and your—

After I stopped working with Mingus in 1972 maybe, it became a little rough. Mingus did work a lot and it was easier for me, but when I started working with my own group or being on my own, it was harder. So there was period, probably in the middle to late, I would say late 60s, it was meager. But then things got better.
